searchText: Was ACD cancelled this week? Yes, it's Christmas Eve Oh, right, that is today isn't it? <timbeiko> Warmed my heart that I got an email from Zoom saying Micah was in the meeting 🎄 Merry Christmas everyone! I don't know about you all, but I certainly have nothing better going on at 22:00 on December 24th. Merry Christmas to all of you, and a small present https://medium.com/@vorot93/meet-akula-the-fastest-ethereum-implementation-ever-built-58eaca244c39 🎄 🥳 I'd be curious if you could provide a similar table with geth as a column, and 16 GiB of RAM. I’d be curious too, but I’m not sure if non-Erigon-family nodes can fully validate (a.k.a. not fast/warp/snap sync) in reasonable amount of time and especially disk space On the same boat: in front of a monitor with three different gdb sessions debugging assembler... Giving up right now though and opening a bottle of wine hallo i did that tests on Erigon and Akula, this september I ran a Go Ethereum instance with -syncmode=full, almost the same as Erigon pruned mode on a 16GB machine with NVME memory. geth took 7days and circa 18hours to reach the tip of the chain erigon 2 days and circa 13h to do the same with less footprint (600gb) I didn't even try to synchronize geth in full archivial node because I don't have 7 terabytes (maybe I need more) of disk space and it would have taken a month anyway. To give an idea, currently Erigon on a machine with 16Gb of Ram synchronizes in full archivial node (that is the deafult mode of Erigon) between 79 and 80 hours 3 days and 8 hours, and consumes 1.55Tb of disk space for chain data. In "Snap sync" mode, i.e. without transaction validation by execution but with download of states, geth is obviously extremely fast. For now Erigon does not yet have its own synchronization system for downloading states, i.e. without validating them by execution. When we get it I will do more comparative testing.
